reflection_items.detail: The computed price_shape metric shows adjusted close rising from 10.44 on 2025-01-10 to 24.37 on 2025-09-29, a 133.4291% return over 180 trading days, with daily volatility 2.6198% and a max drawdown of -13.581%. The prediction cited this momentum as a reason a further repricing toward 47.964 was possible. A testable hypothesis is that trailing momentum was treated as evidence of a forward doubling path when no forward projection to 47.964 was supplied. Test by comparing surge calls that cite only trailing returns against those with an explicit forward path, and by checking whether the doubling threshold was ever bridged.
limitations: This is a hypothesis about the reasoning process, not an established cause of the outcome.

reflection_items.brief: For future surge calls on this case, require the surge case to state a concrete forward path to the 47.964 doubling threshold and to record the overbought/valuation counter-evidence alongside it.
reflection_items.detail: The prediction-time baseline mean adjusted close was 23.982 (recent close 24.37 on 2025-09-29), so the doubling threshold was 47.964. The original prediction itself noted InvestingPro flagged the stock as overbought after a 149.43% one-year change and that no explicit forward projection or price target supported a doubling, yet still returned 'possible' surge. Action: when a surge call is made, require (a) a stated forward path or catalyst sequence that could plausibly reach the doubling threshold within the horizon, and (b) explicit recording of the strongest counter-evidence (overbought conditions, prior-year run-up, growth-deceleration risk). This is an optional analytical discipline, not a mandatory price-proof gate, and it does not by itself determine the binary judgment.
limitations: Requiring a forward path is a process discipline; it does not guarantee correct binary classification.
The overbought and growth-deceleration observations are third-party commentary, not validated causal factors.
This action must not be treated as a binding price-proof condition for a positive judgment.
